To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HERMES data provide access to the generalized form factors of the proton.

the data on DVCS and deeply virtual meson production are in agreement with theoretical predictions based on generalized parton distributions and the QCD factorization theorem, and that the HERMES data on DVCS are essential in this context.
we have shown that HERMES data allow to map the space of Comptons form factors, and that we have shown the existence of the so-called GPDs in the framework of the collinear twist-2 approximation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extraction of GPDs and CFFs from experimental data.
the extraction of generalized parton distribution and Compton form factor in the framework of a generalized parton model.
a systematic analysis of HERMES data in terms of the GPDs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are not conclusive, and we are not there yet.
the experimental data are consistent with GPDs being the underlying physics.
the data are not yet precise enough to draw a definite conclusion on the shape of the generalized parton distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to extract a number of generalized form factors from the data, but that the quality of the data is still not sufficient to determine all of them.
we have shown the feasibility to determine the Compton form factors from the HERMES data.
the data are in agreement with the GPD model calculations, but the data are not precise enough to discriminate among different models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HERMES data are crucial for a precise determination of the GPDs.
HERMES data are essential for the extraction of the generalized transversity distribution, as well as the generalized Boer-Mulders function.
the HERMES data provide a unique opportunity to constrain the Compton form factors and to extract the generalized parton distributions in a wide region of the kinematic space.
